decisions.reason: As a standard perfect binder it fits the core finishing portfolio and can be kept at relatively low cost, though overlap with the fully automatic model raises the chance of later pruning if demand proves weaker.
The fully automatic perfect binder matches the firm's stated move toward automation and productivity, so real-options logic favors retaining it absent clear negative market evidence.
An inline/nearline booklet maker aligns well with digital print finishing and complementary service sales, making it worthwhile to keep the option open while market demand remains plausible.
